question: Rakesh invests a sum of ₹5,000 and Shivam invests a sum of ₹9,000 at the same rate of simple interest per annum. If, at the end of 3 years, Shivam gets ₹360 more interest than Rakesh, then find the rate of interest per annum (in percentage).
solution:
**Given:**

Principal invested by Rakesh (PR) = ₹5,000

Principal invested by Shivam (PS) = ₹9,000

Time (t) = 3 years

Difference in interest = ₹360

**Formula used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = P × r × t / 100

Difference in interest = SIS - SIR

**Calculations:**

SIS = PR × r × t / 100

SIR = PS × r × t / 100

Difference in interest = ₹360

⇒ (PS × r × t) / 100 - (PR × r × t) / 100 = ₹360

⇒ r × t × (PS - PR) / 100 = ₹360

⇒ r × 3 × (₹9,000 - ₹5,000) / 100 = ₹360

⇒ r × 3 × ₹4,000 / 100 = ₹360

⇒ r × ₹12,000 / 100 = ₹360

⇒ r × ₹120 = ₹360

⇒ r = ₹360 / ₹120

⇒ r = 3%

**∴ The rate of interest per annum is 3%, and the correct answer is option (2).**
